attempts.raw_response: The vessel then underwent extensive trials in the North Sea to test its systems and propulsion. During one such trial in 2017, a fault was discovered in the port gearbox, requiring repairs that delayed the programme. HMS Queen Elizabeth was officially commissioned in December 2017, with Her Majesty The Queen presiding over the ceremony. The carrier can operate a range of aircraft including the F-35B Lightning II fighter jets and Merlin helicopters. Its air wing is expected to number up to 40 aircraft. The ship forms the centerpiece of the Royal Navy's new carrier strike capability and represents the largest warship ever built for the British navy. A second carrier, HMS Prince of Wales, is also now in service.

pair.human_continuation: It is the first of two new carriers being delivered by the Aircraft Carrier Alliance. The second, HMS Prince of Wales, is currently under construction at shipyards across the UK before it too is assembled at Babcock's Rosyth Dockyard. Programme director Ian Booth said: "These new images show really clearly how far this programme has come. We are well on the way towards delivering a world-class aircraft carrier that will represent the UK globally for the next 50 years. "By the end of this year HMS Queen Elizabeth will be fully assembled and we are already looking forward to her launch in 2014. "There are thousands of skilled men and women working on this programme and they should all feel proud of what they are accomplishing."
pair.prefix: And all that remains to be fitted to the ship are two sponsons - flight deck extensions - and the ramp or "ski-jump"' which give aircraft an extra boost on take-off. The "aft island" was the final section to arrive at Rosyth and was constructed in 90 weeks by workers at BAE Systems' yard in Scotstoun, Glasgow. When complete and fully fitted out HMS Queen Elizabeth will weigh 65,000 tonnes.

source_document.title: Royal Navy's latest aircraft carrier nears completion at Rosyth
